summary: 1. Anchor topics to intimate human sensory experiences (bodily sensations, food eating you, hidden biology) rather than inanimate physical objects or roadside engineering. 2. Open with an immediate, declarative paradox under 14 words that challenges intuition rather than explaining the answer in line one. 3. Stop using questions as opening hooks ('Why do...' or 'Ever noticed...'), which tank stayed percentage below 40%. 4. Eliminate generic reaction emojis (🤯, 🤔) and academic title phrasing; use two visceral, concrete nouns with topic-specific emojis (e.g., 🍍👅, 💧🧽). 5. Kill countdown timers and lengthy explanatory clauses ('...because it stores very little heat'), which leak viewers before the 3-second mark.
winning_hooks: Your fingers prune in water, but it is not because you are absorbing it like a sponge.
Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back.
Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.
This shark is older than the United States.
avoid: Opening by asking a rhetorical question: 'Why do car windows shatter into tiny cubes?'
Casual conversational setups: 'Ever noticed those tiny black dots fading around your car windshield?'
Giving the scientific explanation away inside the first sentence: '...because it stores very little heat' or '...because its defense chemicals work differently'
Abstract or passive title formats: 'How Acorns Indirectly Affect Lyme Disease Rates 🤯'
Overlay countdown timers on Shorts under 45 seconds (strongly correlated with sub-40% stayed rates)
next_experiment: A/B test an identical 25-second script on bodily phenomena (e.g., 'Brain Freeze') using Hook A (Declarative Paradox: 'Your brain freeze has nothing to do with your brain.') vs Hook B (Curiosity Question: 'Why does ice cream give you sudden brain freeze?') to isolate whether question-based phrasing is the primary driver swiping viewers away.
